title: Stepwise latency jumps from microbatch misallocation — hypothesis, experiments, and guardrail implementation
creator: Ava Chen
description: This ticket captures investigation and follow-up work for a production incident where p95/p99 latency exhibited stepwise jumps under moderate concurrent load. The behavior traces to microbatch sizing and a scheduler misallocation that routed tiny microbatches to a high-latency kernel variant in certain conditions. Scope: reproduce reliably in staging, validate root cause hypothesis, implement short-term mitigation (deterministic fallback / circuit), and ship a long-term guardrail to prevent recurrence without regressing throughput.
incident_summary: INC-2025-013: Beginning 2025-02-09 16:12 UTC, customers observed intermittent 2–4x p95 latency spikes for gen endpoints. Spikes correlated with bursts from a single tenant route and an increased proportion of sub-8-token microbatches. Symptoms lasted ~90 minutes; mitigation rolled at 16:48 UTC reduced spikes.
root_cause: Interaction between the microbatch bucketizer and kernel affinity scorer. A recent tweak to the affinity decay constant (commit 7b4f9d) increased preference for 'fused-quant' kernels for energy-efficient execution, but the bucketizer produced many sub-threshold microbatches during client bursts. The affinity scorer's stale prefix KV cache estimate and autotile decision logic preferred a kernel variant that had fixed per-invocation overhead, making small microbatches disproportionately expensive. Result: execution path mismatches and stepwise latency jumps as the scheduler oscillated between kernels during burst ramp-up.

mitigations:
Immediate: forced deterministic kernel selection for microbatches < 16 tokens on gen-1 route (hotfix)
Short-term: add admission control that coalesces adjacent tiny microbatches within 5ms window
Long-term: implement affinity score staleness bounds, add kernel confidence telemetry and a circuit-breaker for oscillation; include canary rollout with traffic shaping

acceptance_criteria:
1) No reproduction of stepwise p95/p99 jumps in staging for representative synthetic bursts.
2) Affinity staleness bound in place and observable metrics (kernel_confidence, kernel_churn_rate) reporting.
3) Canary rollout shows <5% change to throughput and no regression in 99th percentile latency across test fleet.
